title: DEL-trained models identify experimentally active small-molecule hits
summary: Models trained on DNA-encoded-library selection data prioritized roughly 2,000 compounds for biochemical testing across three targets. The study reports active and potent hits outside the training libraries. Human filtering and chemical review contributed to selection. These are biochemical hits, not established safe or effective drugs; the authors disclose commercial interests and related patent applications.
ai_technology: Graph-convolutional neural networks and random forests

evidence.tested: Newly selected compounds were tested in biochemical assays.
evidence.unknown: Cellular efficacy, selectivity, safety and clinical benefit remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: Graph-convolutional neural networks and random forests supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.

source_review.scope: Author-hosted published-article PDF abstract, selected experimental Results, affiliations and disclosures; prior PubMed online date retained.
